messages:
Elena (PM): Quick sync  need a product decision: customers asking for notarized evidence exports (signed by customer key + timestamped notarization), eDiscovery-friendly indexing, and explicit SOC2/ISO artifact bundling. Can we scope a pilot that doesn't blow infra?
Raj (Eng): Short answer: yes, but two pieces add complexity: notarization flow (timestamping service + signature chain) and eDiscovery indexing (inverted index over redacted content) which needs storage+search cost. Pilot alpha: produce signed manifest + optional notarization stamp (timestamp token from TSA) and simple index of metadata only.
Mei (Security): Notarization requires non-repudiation. Recommend customer-supplied JWK for manifest signing, plus a server-side TSA request that returns a timestamp token we include in the manifest. No key escrow. Also require audit trail for who requested export and from which IP.
Priya (Legal): Legal needs a clear definition of "notarized export" in contracts: manifest + signer_kid + TSA_token + per-file sha256 + chain-of-custody log. Also require retention-exception endpoint for legal holds. I'll draft addendum language.
Tom (AE): Customers will pay for indexing if it speeds eDiscovery. Ask: can the index be a separate billable add-on (per-GB indexed)? Also one prospect wants SOC2 attachments zipped into the notarized bundle.
Elena (PM): Proposal for pilot scope:
- Deliverables: signed JSONL snapshots (gz), manifest with per-file sha256, optional TSA_token field for notarization, minimal metadata index (tenant, ts, event_type, redaction_policy).
- Retention lanes: 30d / 1y / 7y (legal hold overrides TTL).
- BYOK: JWK upload -> challenge -> confirm. HSM signing fallback if customer cannot sign.
Raj (Eng): Implementation notes: exporter writes parts -> computes sha256 -> requests TSA for timestamp-token (if notarize=true) -> assemble manifest -> attach signature (customer or HSM). Indexer writes small doc per event for search. We'll surface cost delta.
Mei (Security): Sampling policy: control-plane 100%, content default 5% but customers can opt-in to full content index with a signed capacity addendum. Redaction policy must be explicit; index stores tokenized redacted snippets, not verbatim by default.
Priya (Legal): If we add notarization in pilot, include a manifest acceptance checklist that Sales can sign with customer: items that the export certifies vs what it does not (e.g., sampled content caveats).
cert-bot: Created ticket INFR-8220: "Pilot: notarized evidence exports + eDiscovery index" assigned to Raj (Eng). ETA 6 weeks.
Elena (PM): Action items: Raj - prototype export + TSA integration + cost estimate (10d); Mei - security checklist + sampling caveats (4d); Priya - addendum + manifest acceptance template (3d); Tom - customer confirmation & pricing asks (2d). Reconvene in 9 days. :calendar:,
